bib.title: AgentGym-RL: Training LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Decision Making through Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: AgentGym-RL: Training LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Decision Making through Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning. Zhiheng Xi, Jixuan Huang, Chenyang Liao et al. (Fudan University, ByteDance Seed, Shanghai Innovation Institute). arXiv 2509.08755v1 preprint, September 2025.

COVERAGE: 136,178 of 136,178 chars read, 39 of 39 pages. I read the body, results tables, discussion, conclusion and Appendices A to C (settings, trajectory case studies). I skimmed the references, pp. 21-30, only for origins. Appendix C figure text was read, but the figures themselves were not viewed.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- Claim: RL from scratch with no SFT lifts a 7B open model to roughly the level of frontier proprietary models on 5 environments.
  - number: +33.65 points average gain
  - setup: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, GRPO, five environments (WebArena, Deep Search, TextCraft, BabyAI, SciWorld), in-domain train/test splits.
  - quote: "Open-source models (e.g., Qwen-2.5-7B [83]) trained with our framework and method achieved an average improvement of 33.65 points, matching—or even outperforming—larger commercial, closed-source models such as OpenAI-o3"
  - where: p.3, Introduction

- Claim: A 7B model with ScalingInter-RL beats open models of about 10x its size on average.
  - number: ~58.6% average success rate vs Llama3.1-70B (~47%) and Qwen2.5-72B (~43%)
  - setup: Figure 1 right, overall accuracy across the five environments, ScalingInter-7B.
  - quote: "achieves an average success rate of approximately 58.6% after being trained with our reinforcement learning framework. This performance not only surpasses other open-source models of similar size but also significantly outperforms much larger models like Llama3.1-70B ( 47%) and Qwen2.5-72B ( 43%)"
  - where: p.11, Section 4.2
  - The paper reads the gap as post-training and test-time compute scaling better than parameter scaling, which is an interpretation. It compares one RL-trained 7B with untrained larger models, not equal-compute baselines.

- Claim: ScalingInter-RL raises the max interaction horizon in stages, and this is more stable than a fixed long or short horizon.
  - number: none (qualitative, Figure 7)
  - setup: Deep Search, max rounds 5 vs 10 vs ScalingInter-RL, about 350 training steps.
  - quote: "using a larger maximum interaction turn (e.g., 10) achieves higher performance in the early stage compared to a shorter-turn setting (e.g., 5), but rapidly collapses as training progresses."
  - where: p.11. The Figure 7 caption (p.12) attributes the collapse to "high variance, credit assignment difficulties, and overfitting to spurious behaviors". Short horizons "yield more stable but less exploratory learning, leading to a performance ceiling."
  - Method: h_{t+1} = h_t + δh, updated every Δ steps, with a monotonic schedule h1 < h2 < ... < hn (p.9). The schedule's phase boundaries come from "the total optimization steps of the original RL process" (p.11), with no tuning. No concrete h values or Δ are given in the main text or appendix.

- Claim: ScalingInter-7B results per environment (best of the paper's models).
  - number: WebArena 26.00 (GPT-4o 16.00, o3 34.00, o4-mini 36.00); Deep Search 38.25 (o3 49.50, DeepSeek-R1-0528 40.25, Gemini-2.5-Pro 36.50, GPT-4o 26.75); TextCraft 91.00 (Gemini-2.5-Pro 94.00, o3 93.00); BabyAI 96.67 (o3 94.44); SciWorld 57.00 (o3 41.50).
  - setup: Tables 1-5. Test sets are small: 50 WebArena queries, 400 sampled queries across 7 search datasets, BabyAI sub-tasks of 5 to 15 items.
  - quote: "Our ScalingInter-7B model establishes a new state-of-the-art with an overall score of 57.00, which significantly surpasses all open-source and proprietary models, including the next-best proprietary model, OpenAI o3 (41.50)."
  - where: p.15, Table 5

- Claim: RL gains are largest in rule-clear simulated worlds and moderate in open-ended ones.
  - number: SciWorld 1.50 to 50.50 (AgentGym-RL-7B)
  - setup: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct base vs AgentGym-RL-7B, SciWorld. The ScalingInter run reaches 57.00.
  - quote: "On SciWorld's complex scientific reasoning tasks, our method boosted the model's score from 1.50 to 50.50, an astounding increase of nearly 50 points. In contrast, for more open-ended environments like WebArena and Deep Search, the performance gains from RL were rather moderate"
  - where: p.11
  - Other base-to-RL jumps from the tables: Qwen2.5-3B TextCraft 14.00 to 75.00, Qwen2.5-7B TextCraft 42.00 to 89.00, Qwen2.5-7B BabyAI 66.67 to 92.22 (Tables 3-4).

- Claim: GRPO clearly beats REINFORCE++ in this setup, and 3B GRPO beats 7B REINFORCE++ on TextCraft and BabyAI.
  - number: 3B: TextCraft 75.00 vs 28.00, BabyAI 93.33 vs 70.00, SearchQA 25.75 vs 13.25. 7B: 83.00 vs 73.00, 92.22 vs 84.44, 34.00 vs 24.00.
  - setup: Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct, Table 6. The SearchQA entries (3B 25.75, 7B 34.00) equal the AgentGym-RL-3B/7B scores in Table 2.
  - quote: "its 3B variant achieves higher scores than the 7B REINFORCE++ model. This finding points to a fundamental algorithmic advantage that is more impactful than sheer model scale."
  - where: p.16-18
  - The authors' explanation is that Monte Carlo full-episode returns give high-variance gradients. The text also says GRPO uses "a learned baseline", although GRPO uses a group-relative baseline. No ablation isolates the cause. PPO and RLOO are supported by the framework but not reported.

- Claim: Agent performance rises with test-time interaction turns and with pass@K sampling, and the RL model stays ahead of the base.
  - number: at K=64, +5.5% on Deep Search and +7.05% on SciWorld over the untrained base.
  - setup: Figures 8-9; Deep Search turns 2-10, SciWorld turns 10-30; Pass@K with K from 2^1 to 2^6.
  - quote: "with 64 sampling attempts, our RL model achieves a 5.5% improvement in Deep Search environment and a 7.05% improvement in SciWorld environment over the untrained base model"
  - where: p.16. The curves were read as extracted axis text only, with no values.

- Claim: Specific behaviour changes after RL (qualitative case studies).
  - Base agents loop on dead UI elements (clicking the same element for acts 5 to 15) or repeat movement patterns in BabyAI.
  - RL agents recover from "Page not found", use the search box, and backtrack through doors.
  - Failures remain: in SciWorld the agent swaps factual recall for the experimental procedure, and it ends early after focusing on one animal. In WebArena it over-interacts with redundant clicks, hovers and scrolls.
  - number: none
  - where: Section 5.3, p.17-18; Appendix C, Figs 10-16
  - quote: "the RL agent engages in superfluous interaction patterns—including redundant clicking, unnecessary hovering, and excessive scrolling"

- Claim: Chem-Mix on SciWorld is unsolved by every model, including the RL models.
  - number: 0 for all models (RL models 0.00)
  - quote: "The "Chem-Mix" sub-task proved to be intractable, with every model, including our top performers, scoring zero."
  - where: p.15. This contradicts Table 5, where several models show non-zero values in the Chem-Mix-ish column. The column headers were garbled in extraction, so I cannot verify which column is Chem-Mix.

- Claim: The framework design and engineering choices.
  - Decoupled Environment / Agent / Training modules; each environment is an HTTP server exposing /observation, /available_actions, /step and /reset. Built on veRL and AgentGym.
  - Supports PPO, GRPO, RLOO, REINFORCE++, SFT, DPO and AgentEvol-style rejection sampling.
  - Fixes: a TextCraft crafting_tree memory leak, a SciWorld clock leak, parallel Chromium instances for WebArena, and a full-reset interface for WebArena.
  - number: none
  - where: Section 3, p.5-7

- Claim: Training hyperparameters (Appendix B).
  - number: GRPO, KL coefficient 1e-3, temperature 1.0. Learning rate 5e-7 for WebArena and 1e-6 for the rest. WebArena samples 4 trajectories per query; the rest sample 8. Max turns: WebArena 15, Deep Search 4, TextCraft/BabyAI/SciWorld 20.
  - setup: A100 GPUs and Ascend 910B NPUs. WebArena has 372 train / 50 test queries (Information Seeking and Site Navigation only; Content & Config tasks excluded). SFT baselines use learning rate 1e-4.
  - quote: "We employ GRPO as the main RL algorithm with a learning rate of 5 × 10−7 and a KL cofficient of 1 × 10−3. For each query, we sample 4 distinct trajectories using a temperature of 1.0."
  - where: p.32

LIMITS
- Authors concede the following (Section 7):
  - Agents do well in-domain, and generalisation to new environments and tools is open.
  - Tasks are simple digital ones, with long-horizon physical-world tasks left for future work.
  - It is single-agent only.
- The authors do not show any of the following:
  - No fixed-horizon ablation beyond max-rounds 5 vs 10 vs staged, and only in Deep Search (Fig 7).
  - No reported variance, seeds or confidence intervals.
  - No SFT-baseline results appear in the main tables, although the appendix lists SFT learning rates.
  - No concrete h schedule values.
  - No cross-environment transfer.
  - No compute or cost comparison, though the text says staged scaling "dramatically reduces the computational resources and time required".
- Reward is a binary or partial outcome reward in [0,1]. No process reward or credit-assignment method is tested.
- Test sets are small, so differences of a few points are noise.
- Internal inconsistencies in the paper:
  - Text says AgentGym-RL-7B "achieved an overall score of 16.00%, matching GPT-4o" on WebArena, but Table 1 shows 22.00.
  - The text claims ScalingInter "surpasses the base model by 30 points" on TextCraft. The tables show 91.00 vs 42.00 (+49) for Qwen2.5-7B, and the 30-point figure cannot be reproduced from them.
  - The text says "more than a 10% improvement on WebArena", while Table 1 shows 9.76 to 26.00.
  - Table 4 marks Qwen2.5-72B's 88.89 as an open-source model, and Table 4 is labelled "Open-sourced Models" twice.
- Dated: baselines are mid-2025 (o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-0528), so the "matches frontier" claim has aged.

BUILDS ON (names and years as printed)
- AgentGym (Xi et al. [77]) for environments and the POMDP formulation, and veRL (Sheng et al. [56]) for training infrastructure.
- RL algorithms: PPO (Schulman et al. [53]); GRPO (Shao et al. [54]); REINFORCE++ (Hu 2025 [21]); RLOO (Kool et al. 2019, "Buy 4 REINFORCE samples" [30]); REINFORCE (Williams [73]).
- DeepSeek-R1 (2025) and OpenAI o1 for RL-with-verifiable-rewards and test-time compute scaling.
- Multi-turn RL agent prior work: Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025 [26]); SkyRL-v0 (Cao et al. 2025 [3]), and the "length-scaling" analogy from DeepScaleR (Luo et al. 2025 [37]).
- The closest test-time-compute work is TTI [55] and Zhu et al. [96], "Scaling test-time compute for LLM agents".
- AgentEvol [77] for rejection sampling.
- Environments: WebArena [94], TextCraft [45], BabyAI (Chevalier-Boisvert 2019 [7]), SciWorld [69].

CODE
- Rollout pseudocode (Figure 3, p.5) shows the loop: generate in parallel across envs, then compute log-prob and ref log-prob, compute advantages, update the actor.

```
batch = actor.compute_log_prob(batch)
batch = reference.compute_ref_log_prob(batch)
batch = compute_advantages(batch, method="grpo")
actor.update_actor(batch)
```

- Stage 1 loops `for i in range(max_rounds)`, calls `env.step(response)` in parallel, and breaks when `all_done(handlers)`.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): left, per-environment success of the RL model vs proprietary, open and thinking models; right, accuracy vs parameter count (headline "7B beats 70B").
- Fig 5 (p.8): ScalingInter-RL schematic. It shows the horizon staging explained in the text.
- Fig 6 (p.10): training reward curves per environment. The extraction was garbled.
- Fig 7 (p.12): Deep Search reward and rounds for max-rounds 10, 5 and ScalingInter-RL. It is the one figure that shows the collapse for a large horizon and the ceiling for a short one.
- Fig 8-9 (p.17): test-time turn scaling and Pass@K.
- Fig 10-16 (pp.20, 35-39): trajectory comparisons, base vs RL. Fig 12 (BabyAI door backtracking) and Fig 10 (WebArena click loop vs recovery) explain the behaviour change faster than prose.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction faults: Figure 6 axis labels are garbled (font-encoded text). Table 5 column headers (Measure, Test-Cond., Find, Chem-Mix, Lifespan) do not align cleanly with the values, so per-subtask readings are unreliable. Figure curve values are not recoverable.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- The abstract tail was read as "surpass commercial models on 27 tasks across diverse environments". I did not see the full sentence, so I give "27 tasks" only as a fragment and did not cite it as a claim.
- Working copy of the extraction: /tmp/agentgym.txt.
